text:
Alex R: kicking off bring-up for ap-sg1 (GKE) + ap-south2 (EKS) and a small on-prem kubeadm fallback cluster. goal: gpu-backed inference capacity with fast failover and predictable cost. posting a working checklist, questions inline.
Priya S: 👍 do we have quota confirmed for T4/A10 in ap-sg1? GKE quotas are weird there.
Jamal T: not yet, quota request queued with cloud team. ap-south2 we'll use EKS managed + spot mixed instances for batch. on-prem will be small control-plane + 2 worker racks with A100s for sensitive workloads.
Kate L: we should lock kube version to 1.26.x across all three to avoid kubelet kube-proxy mismatch. also plan CNI: prefer antrea for on-prem and calico on cloud for IPIP/MTU reasons.
Alex R: notes: keeping kube versions consistent. high-level checklist below, then config snippets.
Alex R: CHECKLIST - cluster bootstrap basics:
- confirm cloud GPU quota (T4/A10) and per-project vCPU limits
- create node pools with GPU taint: node-role.kubernetes.io/gpu=true:NoSchedule
- install GPU drivers via bootstrap DaemonSet or image with drivers baked in
- deploy nvidia device plugin + node-feature-discovery
- base addons: metrics-server, cert-manager, kube-proxy (iptables mode), coredns
- CNI: calico on GKE/EKS, antrea on on-prem (MTU 1400 tuning)
- monitoring: prom + node-exporter + dcgm-exporter for GPU metrics
- autoscaler: cluster-autoscaler with spot-aware fallback policy

Priya S: quick command to taint nodes when creating nodepool (GKE):
```bash
# after nodepool created
kubectl taint nodes -l cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool=gpu-pool node-role.kubernetes.io/gpu=true:NoSchedule
```
Jamal T: GPU driver bootstrap snippet (kubeadm/on-prem) - we used this during last rack bringup:
```bash
# run on each worker during image provisioning
apt-get update && apt-get install -y linux-headers-$(uname -r) build-essential
# install nvidia driver from repo
curl -sSL https://us.download.nvidia.com/tesla/515.86.01/nvidia-driver-installer.run | bash
# install kubelet and join token later
```
Kate L: recommend instead using NVIDIA CUDA base images + node feature detection and the nvidia-driver-installer DaemonSet for driver install during bootstrapping unless we control images. less brittle.
Alex R: Device plugin apply (works for both cloud and on-prem):
```bash
kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/k8s-device-plugin/main/nvidia-device-plugin.yml
```
Alex R: GPU capacity check after nodes are Ready:
```bash
kubectl get nodes -o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,GPU:.status.allocatable."nvidia.com/gpu"
```
Priya S: networking gotcha: cloud providers default MTU 1460 but on-prem is 1500. set CNI mtu to 1400 for tunnels (we've seen pod-to-pod latency spikes otherwise).
Jamal T: also ensure IPVS vs iptables mode for kube-proxy; iptables is simpler for hybrid but IPVS gives better perf at scale. decision: start with iptables, revisit if tail latencies increase.
Kate L: security/hardening: RBAC defaults, pod security admission (baseline), restrict hostNetwork on GPU pods, and ensure node auto-upgrade disabled for gpu nodepools.
Alex R: cost control notes:
- EKS spot for batch-worker nodepools with mixed instance types (A10, T4 fallback)
- GKE use committed monthly pool for latency-sensitive models, use preemptible only for cheap batch jobs
- set resourceRequests on GPU pods to avoid binpacking too many bound GPUs per node (request both cpu/memory and requests.k8s.io/gpu)

Priya S: autoscaler config: annotate nodepools with cloud scaling group tags, set expander to least-waste, and configure multiple instance types prioritized by cost/perf.
Jamal T: handoff items for oncall/SRE:
- runbook link (placeholder): /runbooks/region/ap-sg1-gke-bootstrap (will upload)
- smoke tests: create job that runs a small inference client hitting model endpoint, verify 99p latency < 300ms and GPU utilization spikes then falls back smoothly
- alerting: kubelet memory pressure, GPU temperature >85C, node NotReady >5m, pod GPU scheduling failures

Kate L: ops-bot: start cluster bootstrap job for ap-sg1? @ops-bot we need a deploy job to create nodepool and apply base addons.
ops-bot: cluster-bootstrap started for ap-sg1/gpu-pool (job id cb-2026-07). logs at https://ci.redwood/infrastructure/jobs/cb-2026-07 · :gear:
Alex R: will follow up with exact IaC snippets (Terraform modules) and upload kubeadm join tokens securely to vault. tagging @Priya S and @Jamal T for quota and autoscaler config.
Priya S: I'll escalate quota with GCP and pin a contact in cloud support.
Jamal T: I'll prepare the spot instance mix and test scale-up in staging tomorrow.
Kate L: planning a quick 30m sync after initial bootstrap is done to validate addons + mtus + GPU metrics. :calendar:
Alex R: thanks all. dropping final checklist to ops channel after sync. :thumbsup:
